en.bestFor: Having one character face the camera full-length and read your own script — announcements, quick updates or presenter-style messages where the outfit and stance should stay visible.
en.structure: The script is split into 1 to 20 short clips, about one clause each (around 4 seconds of speech) so the subtitle stays large. A short line still plays for at least 5 seconds.
en.hook: No separate hook is added — the video opens straight on the character saying your first sentence, so lead with your strongest line.
en.arc: Follows your script sentence by sentence in order; each clip carries straight on from the previous one without restaging.
en.narrator: Exactly one character reads every line aloud to camera. Your script is used word for word; your separate instruction only guides tone and emphasis and is never spoken.
en.visual: Look and palette come from the chosen visual style. One locked full-body shot with the character centered and looking straight into the lens like a real person filming a reel; the same background, lighting and camera angle throughout. While speaking the head, both hands, and whole body keep moving (weight shift, torso sway). Feet stay in frame.
en.audio: No background music — just the character's voice, with a large subtitle that matches each clip's spoken line exactly. It fades and slides in at the start of the clip and fades and slides out at the end. On a 9:16 Instagram Reel the subtitle sits a little below center. On a 16:9 landscape frame it sits at the bottom.
en.rules: Needs a script, one character image and an aspect ratio. Words are never rewritten. Each clip is one short line so the subtitle stays large. The camera does not jump between the start still and the end still. A script over 240 seconds must be shortened.
